pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/36073

This is this feature https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/911 I've implemented the spec I worked on in https://github.com/whatwg/dom/pull/919 and ported the WPTs from https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/26472 

This is following implementations from Chrome and Firefox and positive signals regarding the spec. I am happy to put this behind an experimental warning if you think that's a good idea.

Ping @jasnell

pr_comments: Kind of embarrassing that all the browsers are going to have this feature before us 😅  Though I am happy to wait a few more days for the whatwg/dom PR to be merged if that's a concern.
This pull request lands cleanly on v14.x-staging, but I think the `EventTarget` constructor is not exposed, so I don't know how if we should adapt the tests somehow or just don't land it.

@targos I think it's fine not to land given `EventTarget` is not exposed though it's also fine to land (no harm) in order to make backporting future stuff easier. As you noted the constructor is not exposed so there should not be any user impact.

issue_context.title: RFC - EventTarget API Enhancements
comments: This is definitely interesting and useful. The spec will need to cover the full lifecycle including when the EventTarget unsubscribes from the signal but that's straightforward. Off the top of my head I can't think of any issues with this so I'd say go for it.

review_comments: @addaleax - can you please confirm it's ok (conceptually) that it's fine we don't call `kNewListener` and `kRemoveListener` in this case? I think it should be fine because workers only use this for reference counting but I want to make sure there aren't additional cases I haven't considered.
Yeah, short-circuiting like this this should be okay as far as workers are concerned :+1:
This is in order to fix an unrelated bug where we cache the next handler in our `dispatchEvent` and still call it. Added a test or this case below.

I think that’s reasonable here, yes… it’s way more common to think that you need a weak listener than it is to actually need one, so I wouldn’t expose this as public API, but for internal usage this sounds good :)
My only concern there would be the potential additional performance cost. If the dispatch only incurs that cost for weak handlers then I'm definitely +1
